# Astra reference classification decision policy

## Provenance and evidence

These 163 labels were authored by the assigned Astra agent using the supplied `source_records.json`, the user's seven-category guidelines, and the exact category codes in `scripts/paper_categories.py`. Each full abstract was read in batches. Previous model outputs, checkpoints and evaluations were not consulted; no Ollama, other labeling model, external pages or unseen full texts were used. The small `author_labels.py` script serializes manually authored decisions and validates them; it does not infer labels from keywords.

Evidence quotes are exact, contiguous substrings of the supplied abstract, or the title for the ten Preface records with no abstract. An evidence quote supports the decision but does not replace reading the complete abstract. These are reference judgments, not independent confirmation of scientific claims or publication quality. In particular, classification confidence measures fit to the taxonomy, not whether reported performance or physical claims are credible.

## Applied rules

- Identify the principal methodological or system contribution and the outcomes being evaluated. A domain name, the word “novel”, a theorem name, a sensor, or a cloud deployment alone does not establish a category.
- **AI_ALGORITHMS**: a specified new learning component, architecture, loss, search operator, training mechanism, feature-selection procedure, or general optimization contribution. Explicit architectural redesigns can qualify even when their constituent modules already exist. Architectural-combination abstracts with limited details receive Medium, since Applied AI remains plausible.
- **APPLIED_AI**: comparison, fine-tuning, transfer learning, routine feature selection, standard ensemble voting or optimizer-based hyperparameter tuning aimed at a domain outcome. Named frameworks made from existing components do not automatically become algorithmic contributions. Operational LLM use and empirical investigation of AI-supported software work also fit here.
- **NETWORKS_SECURITY_DISTRIBUTED**: primary protocol, routing, caching, distributed aggregation, authentication, data integrity, intrusion detection or cloud-edge offloading objectives. Minor AI optimization components do not override the principal security/network contribution. Strongly specified new model architectures can take AI_ALGORITHMS when architecture is the contribution, as in row 34; a communication estimator adjustment with little general algorithm innovation stays Networks, as in row 149.
- **QUANTUM_INFORMATION**: actual quantum communication/authentication or post-quantum cryptography explicitly described in the abstract. Applied integration of post-quantum cryptography is within the supplied category's scope. Classical quantum-inspired feature transformations are AI, not quantum information. General quantum physics, spacetime or cosmological modeling without a clear information/computation contribution is outside the taxonomy.
- **THEORETICAL_CS**: foundations of computation or formal verification; mathematics in engineering or biomedical simulation is insufficient. The guideline's formal-verification and proof-oriented tie-breaks apply to rows 57 and 133, both marked Medium for their networking/AI alternatives.
- **COMPUTER_ENGINEERING_IOT_EMBEDDED**: concrete hardware, physical IoT usage, antennas/FPGA, or engineering inspection/signal-processing systems. Standalone chemical nanomaterials and power-generation engineering do not qualify solely because they involve sensors or simulation. Algorithmic sensor-network routing/localization is Networks when the contribution concerns network structure and operation.
- **EDTECH_LEARNING_DIGITAL_LIBRARY**: educational outcomes or academic support are primary. Security of educational credentials remains Networks when authentication/privacy is the contribution. “Teaching-learning” and “curriculum” metaphors in general optimizers do not make educational research.
- Reviews and books with sufficient classifiable subject matter receive a category; they are not treated like content-free prefaces. Retraction notices and Preface records have no classifiable research contribution.
- High means a clear primary category supported by sufficient source text. Medium marks substantive boundaries or limited novelty detail. Low marks a weak but defensible fit. `Preface` is the application's historical storage enum for รอตรวจสอบ, not an eighth category: category is null for all such entries. `review_reason` specifies non_research, outside_taxonomy or ambiguous as applicable; Medium alternatives alone do not require review_reason=ambiguous.

## Most consequential boundary decisions

| Source row(s) | Primary judgment | Rationale / competing interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | null / Preface / outside_taxonomy | Empirical software reliability via uncertain differential equations is software engineering, but lacks foundations-of-computation, AI, network, hardware or education contributions that fit these seven categories. It is not a content-free record. |
| 4–5, 21, 36, 61 | Networks / Medium | Cloud load balancing, watermark robustness, network-aware FL or multimedia integrity are the actual system objectives; AI algorithms are plausible alternatives. |
| 10 | Applied AI / Medium | The abstract's four agents use named RL approaches for selecting a small clinical biomarker subset; it does not clearly isolate a new RL learning rule. |
| 13, 17, 19, 26, 72, 95, 102, 106, 108, 122–123, 137–138 | AI algorithms / Medium | Explicit custom or hybrid architectures are presented as the method, but domain focus and reuse of existing modules make Applied AI plausible. These rows are the strongest candidates for a stricter architecture-novelty adjudication. |
| 24, 64, 87, 96, 129, 132 | Applied AI / High or Medium | Applying existing attention, optimization, tag representations or directional domain weights does not by itself demonstrate a new learning algorithm. Rows 24, 87, 129 and 132 retain AI_ALGORITHMS as a substantive Medium alternative. |
| 28, 76 | Networks | Academic credential authentication and privacy are the core contribution; education supplies the deployment setting. |
| 30, 85 | Engineering / Low / ambiguous | Classical signal-processing estimation of imaging motion is computing work adjacent to imaging instrumentation, but the abstracts do not establish a hardware or learned-model contribution. AI_ALGORITHMS is only a weak alternative through broad algorithmic image-analysis scope. |
| 32 | Engineering / Medium | Deterministic PCB optical inspection explicitly has no training phase; it is classified as an engineering inspection method rather than assuming ML. |
| 52 | Engineering / Medium | A physical IoT health-device pilot is evaluated; the study also has substantial welfare/access and acceptance content rather than hardware invention. |
| 57 | Theoretical CS / Medium | Proof of structured optimal routing and polynomial-time linear programming is sufficiently central for the theory tie-break, although programmable-switch networking is a strong alternative. |
| 67 | AI algorithms / Medium | The abstract explicitly says the rotation layer runs on classical hardware, and describes a bounded feature map to stabilize GAN training. |
| 73–74, 151 | Quantum / Medium | Explicit post-quantum cryptography (73–74) or quantum-particle authentication (151) triggers the quantum category; the broader architectures could reasonably be classified as Networks. No external verification of these claims was performed. |
| 99, 111, 118, 124, 131 | AI algorithms / Medium | A new data-quality procedure, multi-metric cost function, layer-weighting strategy, BEL update stabilization, or GAN sampling framework is the methodological focus, even though existing components are reused. |
| 100, 146 | Networks / Medium | Adaptive charger scheduling for network lifetime and hop-based node localization are network-operation methods; embedded/sensor systems is the alternative. |
| 107 | Networks / Medium | A book with a substantive abstract on blockchain, IoE and FL security is classifiable by subject; this is not treated as a Preface. |
| 133 | Theoretical CS / Medium | Formal verification via CPN state spaces and model checking controls the guideline tie-break, while ENGRU architecture makes AI_ALGORITHMS plausible. |
| 140 | Applied AI / Low / ambiguous | Automated ecological image analysis using thresholding/morphology is a weak classical computer-vision application fit, without explicit ML. A strict ML-only interpretation could instead abstain; engineering is also weak. |
| 157 | Quantum / High | The stated subject is entangled-qubit data transmission. High category confidence is not endorsement of the near-faster-than-light claim. |
| 158 | null / Preface / outside_taxonomy | Spacetime/quantum-gravity theory, despite entanglement and proof vocabulary, does not establish quantum computing or communication methods. It is classified from its own abstract, independently of the separate retraction notice. |

## Records requiring review

- **Low, ambiguous**: rows 30, 85, 140.
- **No research contribution**: rows 37–46 are Preface records; row 110 is a retraction notice. (Rows 37–46 contain ten entries.)
- **Outside taxonomy**: rows 3, 31, 148, 156, 158. Row 31 is colloidal chemical SERS detection, row 148 renewable power quality engineering, and row 156 cardiac biochemical differential-equation modeling.

## Validation and totals

All 163 original `(row, scopus_id)` pairs are retained exactly and in source order. IDs and rows are unique. Every category and alternative uses one of the seven exact codes or null; category is null if and only if confidence is Preface. All quotes pass exact substring checks against their declared evidence source. No classification is based on an absent abstract except the clearly titled Preface records.

Confidence totals: High 92; Medium 52; Low 3; Preface 16.
